placements.title: Memory identity derives from content, not caller-supplied ids
placements.frame: When a memory arrives without an explicit id, does the pipeline's slug-generation chain — LLM id-gen call falling back to deterministic slugify — reliably produce a slug and commit the file, and which path actually fires?
placements.why: src-1 sets up the precondition (no explicit id supplied) that triggers the pipeline's slug-generation obligation described in src-2: derive a slug from content via the LLM id-gen call or its deterministic slugify fallback, then commit the file. Together these describe a recurring design subject — how the pipeline guarantees a committable identity for content-only submissions — rather than a one-time fact, so a leaf rather than a position-grain note is warranted. No existing narrative leaf or strata category covers id/slug-generation fallback behavior, and nothing supplied is close enough to warrant an 'inspired' lineage edge, so this mints standalone.
